transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is I can’t stay on track. I’ll try to do something simple, like work on an application, and then some little noise outside, my phone, or even just a random thought will pull me away. A lot of times I don’t even notice I’ve gotten off track until I’m already doing something else.
Did you have this same kind of trouble staying focused when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. In elementary school it was already a problem. Teachers would move my seat a lot because I’d talk out of turn or get distracted. I’d forget homework, too, and when we had worksheets I’d rush through them and make dumb mistakes even if I knew the material.
Do you have this same trouble staying focused in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yeah, it happens in both places. Like at home I’ll try to sit down and work on an application or something, and then a car outside, my phone, or just some random thought pulls me away. It’s the same kind of thing anywhere, really—I’m off doing something else before I even realize I lost focus.
Have you been feeling down or depressed معظم الأيام?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I have bad days, but I haven’t noticed feeling depressed most days, no.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal stuff sometimes, but I haven’t noticed myself worrying a lot when there’s nothing really going on.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent pattern of inattention beginning in childhood and continuing into adulthood across multiple settings. Confirmed symptoms include easy distractibility, difficulty sustaining attention, forgetfulness with homework, and careless mistakes. Functional impact is suggested in school and current task completion. Depression and generalized anxiety were not supported as primary explanations in the interview.
